experiment: MLSys 2027 Experiment 4 -- matched BF16 vs native FP8-E4M3 vs RABIT-KV physical capacity and latency (mirrored A1 B1 C1 C2 B2 A2)
derivation: Derived from bf16_deployment.log, fp8_e4m3_deployment.log, rabit_kv2_deployment.log, modal_session.log (environment, model snapshot, post-run GPU state), correctness_gate.log, manifest.json, integrity_check.json and matched_config_diff.json. The runner's matched_capacity_latency_summary.json is not a source (validator cross-check only). p90 = statistics.quantiles(values, n=10, method='inclusive')[8]. Pooled = both legs of one dtype only. Signed deltas are x - y on pooled statistics. Range overlap uses the raw sample min/max of the two legs of a dtype.

scope.capacity: PHYSICAL real-engine vLLM allocator KV capacity (num_gpu_blocks x block_size)
scope.latency: PHYSICAL real-engine single-request latency (batch size one; one request per generate call)
scope.session: one matched H100 session (one Modal container, one GPU, fresh engine process per leg)
scope.not_logical: These are NOT logical fake-quant memory figures.

native_fp8_notes.evidence_type: source/config-derived: the audited vllm-kvquant source sets k/v/q scales to 1.0 when the checkpoint has no quantization_config and calculate_kv_scales is False, and on CUDA converts the query to FP8 for fp8/fp8_e4m3 KV caches. The scale tensors and the query dtype were not observed at runtime (the worker makes no engine RPC).

notes: Scope: PHYSICAL real-engine vLLM allocator capacity (num_gpu_blocks x block_size) and PHYSICAL real-engine single-request latency (batch size one), measured in one matched H100 session, eager mode, Triton backend, 2048-token prompt, 32 generated tokens, 5 excluded warmups and 15 measured reps per leg (n=30 pooled per dtype).
This is NOT an FP8 quality comparison and makes no FP8 quality-equivalence claim.
No samples from the earlier BF16-vs-RABIT-KV experiment (Exp3) were reused: BF16, native FP8 and RABIT-KV were all measured fresh in this session.

Findings apply specifically to the native vLLM FP8-E4M3 KV-cache path measured here (per-tensor, default unit KV scales for this checkpoint, native query FP8 conversion in the Triton backend) and are not a statement about FP8 methods in general. The default scale and the query conversion are source/config-derived facts, not direct runtime tensor observations.

Measured physical capacity: BF16 393,024 tokens (12,282 x 32), native FP8 785,568 tokens (24,549 x 32), RABIT-KV 2,074,592 tokens (64,831 x 32); duplicate capacities are identical in both legs of every dtype.
Native FP8 nearly doubles physical capacity relative to BF16 (FP8/BF16 1.9988x); RABIT-KV provides substantially more physical capacity than native FP8 (RABIT/FP8 2.6409x; RABIT/BF16 5.2785x).
Pooled TPOT median: native FP8 17.268 ms vs BF16 15.336 ms; native FP8 is slower than BF16 (+1.933 ms, +12.60%).
Pooled TPOT p90: native FP8 17.502 ms vs BF16 16.632 ms; native FP8 is slower than BF16 (+0.870 ms, +5.23%).
Pooled TTFT median: native FP8 62.378 ms vs BF16 59.649 ms; native FP8 is slower than BF16 (+2.730 ms, +4.58%).
Pooled wall median: native FP8 597.733 ms vs BF16 534.288 ms; native FP8 is slower than BF16 (+63.445 ms, +11.87%).
Native FP8 is slower than BF16 in all four pooled latency metrics of this session (a latency overhead, not a speedup).
Pooled TPOT median: RABIT-KV 20.383 ms vs BF16 15.336 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than BF16 (+5.047 ms, +32.91%).
Pooled TPOT p90: RABIT-KV 20.495 ms vs BF16 16.632 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than BF16 (+3.863 ms, +23.22%).
Pooled TTFT median: RABIT-KV 116.495 ms vs BF16 59.649 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than BF16 (+56.846 ms, +95.30%).
Pooled wall median: RABIT-KV 748.069 ms vs BF16 534.288 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than BF16 (+213.780 ms, +40.01%).
RABIT-KV is slower than BF16 in all four pooled latency metrics of this session (a latency overhead, not a speedup).
Pooled TPOT median: RABIT-KV 20.383 ms vs native FP8 17.268 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than native FP8 (+3.114 ms, +18.04%).
Pooled TPOT p90: RABIT-KV 20.495 ms vs native FP8 17.502 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than native FP8 (+2.993 ms, +17.10%).
Pooled TTFT median: RABIT-KV 116.495 ms vs native FP8 62.378 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than native FP8 (+54.117 ms, +86.76%).
Pooled wall median: RABIT-KV 748.069 ms vs native FP8 597.733 ms; RABIT-KV is slower than native FP8 (+150.335 ms, +25.15%).
RABIT-KV is slower than native FP8 in all four pooled latency metrics of this session (a latency overhead, not a speedup).
No speedup is claimed: no pairwise pooled latency delta in this session is negative.

Order effect BF16 A1 -> A2: TPOT median -4.73% (15.998 -> 15.241 ms; sample ranges [15.352, 16.766] vs [15.083, 15.320] do not overlap); TTFT median -2.09% (60.347 -> 59.087 ms; sample ranges [59.172, 62.232] vs [58.878, 59.670] overlap); wall median -4.46% (555.858 -> 531.088 ms; sample ranges [534.857, 581.274] vs [526.284, 533.719] do not overlap).

Order effect native FP8 B1 -> B2: TPOT median +1.57% (17.172 -> 17.442 ms; sample ranges [16.901, 17.275] vs [17.203, 17.577] overlap); TTFT median -0.05% (62.390 -> 62.358 ms; sample ranges [61.875, 62.958] vs [62.065, 62.736] overlap); wall median +1.33% (594.756 -> 602.676 ms; sample ranges [586.241, 597.911] vs [595.405, 607.217] overlap).
The BF16 order effect remains visible and is not corrected for: BF16 TPOT median drift -4.73% between its two legs, whose sample ranges do not overlap.

The frozen RABIT-KV correctness gate passed before any leg: pytest 105 passed / 14 warnings, prep exactness 62/62, full-attention exactness passed, fast decode-append exactness over 202 state/byte steps.
Integrity: 146 passed, 0 failed, 0 not_run, 0 not_evaluated; matched config passed; protected paths clean.
